column1: # comment: AI-READI clinical_data/condition_occurrence.csv items mapped to MONDO. Subjects are b2ai:<omop_table>.<redcap_variable>. The OMOP table qualifier is mandatory, not cosmetic - these same variables also appear in observation.csv, where they are a self-reported yes/no answer rather than an asserted condition, so the two senses need distinct ids. Subjects are NOT keyed on concept_id, which is not unique per item. Item keys and concept ids come from the VUMC synthetic AI-READI release (data/synthetic/aireadi/); subject_label is the untruncated label from AI-READI's published CC-BY-4.0 crosswalk, because condition_source_value in the data is hard-truncated at 49 characters and is never usable as a label. That crosswalk is a candidate generator and never an oracle - it carries codes that do not resolve, e.g. LOINC:2403450 for systolic blood pressure - so every object_id here was independently found by searching the pinned MONDO release with oaklib and re-verified id->label. Four of the 30 items are deliberately absent -- three are conflated "A or B" checkboxes that must not broadMatch one sense (mhoccur_ua urinary-infection-or-incontinence, mhoccur_cvdot pacemaker-or-valve-disease-or-surgery, mhoccur_circ arterial-or-venous), and mh_a1c reports a lab finding rather than a diagnosis and belongs in an HPO layer. See docs/mapping-conventions.md.

column8: the item asks about "High blood cholesterol" (hypercholesterolemia); MONDO has no hypercholesterolemia term and hyperlipidemia subsumes it

item conflates arthritis with joint pain ("Arthritis (joint pain)"); arthropathy has the exact synonym "Joint disorder" and subsumes both senses, so it is broader than the item rather than one sense of it
the item asks "Cataracts (in one or both eyes)", i.e. cataract generally; the OMOP concept name "Bilateral cataracts" is narrower than what was asked
item is "Cancer (any type)" and MONDO:0004992 is malignant neoplasm, so the scope matches
item is "Chronic pulmonary (lung) problems"; MONDO has no chronic-specific lung term, so the general term is broader than the item
item is the residual category "Other neurological conditions"; the ontology term subsumes it
the item asks "Glaucoma (in one or both eyes)"; laterality is not part of the concept
item is "Diabetic retinopathy (in one or both eyes)"
item is mild cognitive impairment; MONDO has no MCI term (searched "mild cognitive impairment", "cognitive impairment", "cognitive decline"), so the general term is broader
the item is "Dementia (Examples: Alzheimer's Disease...)" - the category, with AD given as an example, so the category term is the match rather than MONDO:0004975 Alzheimer disease
